title: MPH / Hospital Administration (MHA)
kicker: Postgraduate health management and public health

value.body: Two related two-year master's programmes for the health sector. A Master of Public Health (MPH) covers epidemiology, biostatistics, health policy and programme management for population health. A Master of Hospital Administration (MHA, or an MBA in Hospital / Healthcare Management) focuses on running hospitals — operations, quality, finance and health information systems.

items.label: Course length
items.note: Usually includes a field placement or hospital internship

items.label: MHA students enrolled
items.note: Responding institutions; healthcare MBAs counted separately

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A bachelor's degree, usually in a health-related field — MBBS, BDS, AYUSH, nursing, pharmacy, physiotherapy or life sciences; some programmes also accept other graduates. Admission is through the institute's own entrance test and interview, CUET-PG at participating universities, or graduation marks. Some hospital-administration programmes admit only medical graduates.

value.title: At a glance
items: These are small programmes, offered by a limited number of universities and institutes, so seats are few.
Work is found in hospitals, government health programmes, NGOs, research projects and health-tech or insurance firms.
Eligibility differs a lot between institutes, so non-medical graduates need to check each programme.
For doctors, an MD in Community Medicine (via NEET-PG) is a separate, clinical-track route into public health.

value.title: Students enrolled in MPH and MHA
value.note: Programmes with other names (for example MBA in hospital management) are not included. AISHE counts only responding institutions, and coverage varies by year.
value.source: AISHE 2021-22, 2022-23 and 2023-24, Table 11 (programme-wise enrolment, M.P.H. and M.H.A. rows), actual responses (Ministry of Education)
